I hang out on Reddit a lot, and I've always been tired of their bullshit and lack of transparency. I know Reddit is a company out to make money, and that's their goal, but the decisions they are making just seem boneheaded and unreasonable to me. First was the decision to remove the ability to see downvote/upvote counts. That meant if someone posted 'Fuck Niggers' it could be at 10 upvotes and you wouldn't see that 40 people downvoted that comment while 50 upvoted it. Maybe it'd have a dagger on it showing that it's controversial- just kidding. Nobody's ever seen that fucking dagger. Then, if I recall right, fairly recently they decided to do that bullshit font thing. They jacked up the font and told people who didn't like it to 'change the CSS'. Seriously, what an awful decision. Who thinks reddit needs to be read in an extra big and clunky font?

The final straw for me, was the removal of Victoria and the whole Fattening shit. It's been clear for a long time that Reddit doesn't give a fuck about its userbase, but consistently removing subreddits that were only about pictures of fat people, regardless of who created them or the behaviour within, just because the original subreddit broke a rule doesn't make sense to me. They claim to be doing it for 'harassment' but there are many more hateful and harassing subreddits out there, and they chose to take the route of just kicking out the 3 they didn't like. Coontown, SRS, and GasTheKikes are totally cool, but subreddits making fun of fat people are unacceptable? I don't even want to make fun of fat people. I think it's hateful, mean, and cruel to make fun of people who clearly have their own issues in life. But removing a subreddit about fat people hate and not removing subreddits about beating women or hating black people? It just shows that Reddit admins have always had their own personal agenda and what the users want doesn't matter. I knew this for a long time but it was just the straw that broke the camel's back.

Anyway, I'm happy to be here at Voat, and I hope it turns out to be better than reddit.

Hello. Today I'd like to take a bit of time to talk about why I feel I could make a good moderator and what I'd like to see for the future of this community. Starting off, I'm HovrG. I have been playing Smash Bros 'competitively' since SSBB was first released and I was an avid fan of SSBM for a long while before that. I currently have been attending two weeklies in the funshine state of Florida (that hyperbolic time chamber hype!).

I don't want to make this too long, but I think that the subverse is doing fine for the most part. If it stays as a small discussion based community I'd be fine with that. This appeals to more hardcore fans and can seem scary to new players. That being said; I really do like memes and puns and less structured jokes about how the games in general. It would be a shame to shove those parts of the communities off into their own corner. I'm not going to say that memes and such should be unregulated posts and links to image macros. I would strive to integrate them into a a more relaxed discussion. This could mean a weekly thread for all the topical smash humor (maybe link it in the side bar to keep the sticky free?). It could also be a thread that is started by a joke and then asks a question. These can help people who might be more casual join into discussions.

The last point I'd like to quickly give my opinion on is how to promote multi-game technical discussion. I can see this coming in the form of a contest. One of the moderators picks a technical aspect of one of the games and then challenges the community to master and expand on it. I can see some of those fancy flare icons people love so much being given to winners. In the end people learn more as players here.

Thanks for joining me for this post today,

--HovrG
